mainTopic: Which מנחות need הגשה, and the source for each one: the מנחת חוטא, the מנחת סוטה, the מנחת העומר, and others
overview: This amud asks which מנחות need הגשה, being brought near to the corner of the מזבח. The ברייתא first tries to prove by logic that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה, using a הצד השוה from the מנחת נדבה and the מנחת סוטה. That proof breaks down, so the rule comes from the פסוק ״את המנחה״. רבי שמעון then learns the מנחת העומר from ״והבאת״ and the מנחת סוטה from ״והקריבה״, since every logical attempt for the סוטה fails. רבי יהודה learns the סוטה from ״והבאת״ and says the עומר needs no פסוק, because a הצד השוה from the מנחת חוטא and the מנחת סוטה proves it. The two argue over whether the עומר counts as a 'common' offering. The ברייתא next shows that ״אלה״ limits private מנחות to the five kinds, and that ״מאלה״ lets someone who vowed 'a מנחה' bring just one kind. Finally, רבי שמעון includes the מנחות of non-Jews and women in הגשה, but excludes שתי הלחם, לחם הפנים and the מנחת נסכים. The amud ends by asking why the מנחת נסכים is the one excluded, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Comparing the obligatory offering to the voluntary one
steps.stepSummary: The word 'bringing' appears both by the obligatory מנחת חוטא and by the voluntary מנחת נדבה. So just as the voluntary one needs הגשה, the obligatory one does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bringing' is said here about an obligatory meal offering, and 'bringing' is said about a voluntary meal offering. Just as the voluntary one needs הגשה, so too the obligatory one needs הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers its first proof that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה. It does this by linking it to the מנחת נדבה through a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses a form of 'bring' for both offerings. Since the מנחת נדבה definitely needs הגשה, the ברייתא wants to pass that rule over to the מנחת חוטא, which is a מנחת חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the מנחה near to the southwest corner of the מזבח
An obligatory meal offering, one a person must bring
A voluntary meal offering, one a person chooses to bring
'Just as … so too …': the standard way of passing a rule from one case to another

phrases.english: (bringing is said here about) an obligatory meal offering,
and 'bringing' is stated about a voluntary meal offering.
Just as a voluntary meal offering requires bringing near,
so too an obligatory meal offering requires bringing near!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מִנְחַת נְדָבָה טְעוּנָה הַגָּשָׁה אַף מִנְחַת חוֹבָה טְעוּנָה הַגָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's derivation, which began before this section
steps.raayaObject: That the מנחת חוטא requires הגשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'bringing' used for both the מנחת חובה and the מנחת נדבה

steps.title: The voluntary offering has oil and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is challenged. The מנחת נדבה is more special because it has oil and frankincense, which the מנחת חוטא does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the voluntary meal offering? It is special because it requires oil and frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the first proof by pointing out a difference between the two offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the מנחת נדבה needs הגשה only because it is a more 'complete' offering, with oil and frankincense. The מנחת חוטא has neither, so the rule may not carry over to it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about … since it …': a formula for pointing out how the source case is different
Oil and frankincense placed on most meal offerings
A refutation that breaks a comparison by showing a difference

phrases.english: What about a voluntary meal offering?
It is special in that it requires oil and frankincense!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת נְדָבָה שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנָה שֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the comparison made in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the מנחת חוטא to the מנחת נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case has a stricter feature, oil and frankincense, that the target case lacks. So the rule of הגשה may depend on that feature.

steps.title: The סוטה's offering proves oil is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת סוטה has no oil or frankincense, yet it still needs הגשה. So oil and frankincense are not what causes the need for הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The meal offering of a סוטה will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge by bringing a new example, the מנחת סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת סוטה has no oil and no frankincense, just like the מנחת חוטא, but it does need הגשה. This shows that oil and frankincense are not the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley meal offering brought by a woman suspected of unfaithfulness
'Will prove': a case that shows the suggested difference does not matter

phrases.english: The meal offering of a סוטה will prove it!
phrases.notes: Her מנחה has no oil or frankincense either, yet it still needs הגשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That oil and frankincense are what make הגשה necessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת סוטה needs הגשה without oil or frankincense, so that feature does not decide it

steps.title: The סוטה's offering has waving
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת סוטה is also special, because it needs תנופה (waving), and the מנחת חוטא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the meal offering of a סוטה? It is special because it requires waving.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the new example by pointing to its own special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה because it also needs תנופה. The מנחת חוטא has no תנופה, so the proof from the סוטה is weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving the offering back and forth before ה'

phrases.english: What about the meal offering of a סוטה?
It is special in that it requires waving!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת סוֹטָה שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנָה תְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proof from the מנחת סוטה in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the מנחת סוטה as the source for the מנחת חוטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנחת סוטה has a unique requirement, תנופה, which may be the real reason it needs הגשה

steps.title: The voluntary offering proves waving is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת נדבה needs no תנופה, yet it still needs הגשה. So תנופה is not the deciding factor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The voluntary meal offering will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by going back to the מנחת נדבה, which has no waving but still needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example now covers the other's weak spot. The מנחת נדבה shows that תנופה is not needed for הגשה, just as the סוטה showed that oil is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A unique feature of one case that could explain its rule

phrases.english: The voluntary meal offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: It needs no waving, yet it still needs הגשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That תנופה is what makes הגשה necessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת נדבה needs הגשה without תנופה, so that feature does not decide it

steps.title: The common feature: both need a handful, so both need bringing near
steps.stepSummary: Neither example is exactly like the other. But both share קמיצה and הגשה, so the מנחת חוטא, which shares קמיצה, also needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that both need קמיצה and both need הגשה. So I will bring the sinner's meal offering, which is like them in needing קמיצה, and say it should be like them in needing הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא combines both examples into a הצד השוה argument and concludes that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example's special feature is ruled out by the other example, so no special feature can explain the rule. What remains is the feature they share, קמיצה, which goes together with הגשה. The מנחת חוטא has קמיצה too, so it gets הגשה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The argument has returned': we go back to building the rule
'This case is not like that one': each source has its own different feature
The common feature shared by two source cases
Removing a handful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
The meal offering brought by a poor sinner in place of an animal

steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה works when two examples each have a weak spot that the other does not share. Here the מנחת נדבה and the מנחת סוטה are combined to suggest that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה. The next step finds a hole in this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the argument failed when it says 'וחזר הדין'. It means the argument goes back to its goal, now built on two examples together instead of one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of the הצד השוה method of learning. Because this proof is knocked down in step 7, the מנחת חוטא's הגשה ends up coming from the פסוק את המנחה in step 8.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around:
the feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
and the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one.
The common feature between them
is that they are alike in needing a handful removed, and alike in needing bringing near.
I too will bring the sinner's meal offering,
which is like them in needing a handful removed,
so it should be like them in needing bringing near!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the two examples from steps 1 through 5 into one combined proof
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A הצד השוה from the מנחת נדבה and the מנחת סוטה is proposed for the מנחת חוטא's הגשה. It is refuted in step 7.

steps.title: The shared feature does not fit the sinner's offering
steps.stepSummary: The צד השוה of מנחת נדבה and מנחת סוטה is attacked. Both can come from a rich person or a poor person, but the מנחת חוטא comes only from a poor person.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about what the two have in common? They can come from a rich person just like from a poor person. Can you say the same about the sinner's meal offering, which cannot come from a rich person the way it comes from a poor person?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the conclusion of Step 6. It finds something that the מנחת נדבה and the מנחת סוטה share but the מנחת חוטא does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה only works if the shared feature is the only relevant thing. Here the two examples share one more feature: anyone can bring them, rich or poor. The מנחת חוטא is brought only by a poor sinner, so maybe that is why it does not need הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The common feature: a proof built on what two different examples share
A rich person
A poor person
They are fit (allowed) to be brought

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the מנחת סוטה is only for poor women. Every סוטה brings it, rich or poor. Only the מנחת חוטא is limited to a poor person.

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them,
since they are fit to come
from a rich person just like from a poor person,
will you say the same about the sinner's meal offering,
which is not fit to come
from a rich person just like from a poor person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the צד השוה conclusion of Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה from מנחת נדבה and מנחת סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two examples share another feature (they can come from rich and poor alike) that the מנחת חוטא lacks. So the proof breaks down.

steps.title: A verse is needed: "the meal offering"
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot prove it, the ברייתא brings a פסוק, "את המנחה", to include the מנחת חוטא in הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "The meal offering."
steps.whatsHappening: The logical proof failed, so the ברייתא falls back on a פסוק that includes the מנחת חוטא in the rule of הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the logic from Steps 1-7 ended in a weak spot. The extra wording "את המנחה" is read as including every kind of מנחה, even the מנחת חוטא.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse teaches (the logic failed, so we need a פסוק)
"The meal offering": the extra wording that includes the מנחת חוטא

steps.whatToRemember: Logic alone could not prove that the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה. That is why the פסוק "את המנחה" is needed.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "The meal offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8. The extra word "the" is what includes the sinner's מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the failed logic of Step 7 with a פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מנחת חוטא needs הגשה because of the פסוק "את המנחה", not because of logic.

steps.title: רבי שמעון adds the עומר and the סוטה offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from "והבאת" that the מנחת העומר needs הגשה. He learns from "והקריבה" that the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה. He backs up each one with a matching פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: "And you shall bring" includes the מנחת העומר in bringing near. And so it says: "You shall bring the עומר, the first of your harvest, to the priest." "And he shall bring it near" includes the מנחת סוטה in bringing near. And so it says: "And he shall bring it near to the altar."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון brings two more מנחות into the rule of הגשה, each from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is linked to the same word used about that offering somewhere else. "Bring" is used about the עומר, and "bring near" is used about the סוטה. That link shows which offering each word comes to include.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
To include
And so it says: a matching פסוק that supports the reading
"And he shall bring it near"

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"And you shall bring":
phrases.notes: These words are from the same section, ויקרא 2:8.

phrases.english: to include the omer offering in bringing near,
and so it says:
"And you shall bring the omer,
the first of your harvest, to the priest,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:10

phrases.english: "And he shall bring it near":
to include the sota's offering in bringing near,
and so it says:
"And he shall bring it near to the altar."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same פסוק to include two more offerings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת העומר (from "והבאת") and the מנחת סוטה (from "והקריבה") both need הגשה.

steps.title: Why do we need a verse for the מנחת סוטה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר. The מנחת חוטא has no תנופה and still needs הגשה, so the מנחת סוטה, which has תנופה, should surely need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it can be learned by logic: if the sinner's meal offering, which does not need waving, needs bringing near, then the מנחת סוטה, which does need waving, surely needs bringing near!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why רבי שמעון needs a פסוק for סוטה. It says a קל וחומר could teach the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה is treated as a sign of a more serious offering. If the 'lighter' מנחת חוטא already needs הגשה, the 'heavier' מנחת סוטה should need it even more. If that works, the פסוק for סוטה would be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is a logical argument: it could be learned without a פסוק
If the lighter case has the rule, the heavier case surely does
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: But it is a logical argument:
If the sinner's meal offering,
which does not require waving,
requires bringing near,
then the sota's meal offering, which requires waving,
isn't it logical that it requires bringing near!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבי שמעון's פסוק for סוטה is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's use of "והקריבה" for the מנחת סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the מנחת חוטא would already teach it, so the פסוק seems extra.

steps.title: The sinner's offering is wheat
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is pushed away. The מנחת חוטא comes from wheat, a better grain, while the מנחת סוטה comes from barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the sinner's meal offering? It comes from wheat!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא breaks the קל וחומר by showing that the מנחת חוטא has its own advantage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'lighter' case really is lighter in every way. The מנחת חוטא is made of wheat, which is more respected than the barley of the סוטה. So maybe the wheat is what makes it need הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat, the finer grain
Barley, the lesser grain (the מנחת סוטה is made from it)

phrases.english: What about the sinner's meal offering?
It comes from wheat!
phrases.notes: The point is the contrast: the סוטה's offering is barley (במדבר 5:15).

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא, שֶׁכֵּן בָּאָה חִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from מנחת חוטא to מנחת סוטה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מנחת חוטא is wheat, so it is not lighter in every way than the barley מנחת סוטה.

steps.title: The מנחת העומר proves it
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת העומר is barley and still needs הגשה, so wheat is not what makes the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מנחת העומר will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by pointing to another offering that is barley and still needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת העומר is made of barley, just like the סוטה's offering, and it needs הגשה (from Step 9). This shows that wheat is not required for הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: another example that disproves the suggested reason

phrases.english: The omer offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: The עומר is barley too, yet it needs הגשה. So the wheat can't be the reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wheat objection of Step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wheat might be what causes the need for הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barley מנחת העומר needs הגשה, so wheat is not the cause.

steps.title: The מנחת העומר has oil and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The counter-example is challenged. The מנחת העומר has שמן and לבונה, and the מנחת סוטה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the מנחת העומר? It requires oil and frankincense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a special feature of the מנחת העומר that the סוטה's offering lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the עומר needs הגשה because it has oil and frankincense. The מנחת סוטה has neither, so the עומר does not prove anything about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil and frankincense, added to most מנחות but not to the סוטה's

phrases.english: What about the omer offering?
It requires oil and frankincense!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר, שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנָה שֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the counter-example of Step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עומר has oil and frankincense, which the מנחת סוטה lacks. So that feature may be why the עומר needs הגשה.

steps.title: The sinner's offering proves it
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת חוטא has no שמן and no לבונה and still needs הגשה, so oil and frankincense are not the cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sinner's meal offering will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to the מנחת חוטא, which has no oil or frankincense and still needs הגשה. This sets up a צד השוה argument between the two examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example now knocks down the other's special feature. The עומר shows wheat isn't needed, and the חוטא shows oil and frankincense aren't needed. This is the same back-and-forth pattern as Steps 2-5, now heading toward a new צד השוה for סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The poor sinner's meal offering, which has no oil and no frankincense

steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the 'one proves the other' pattern seen earlier. It prepares a צד השוה from מנחת חוטא and מנחת העומר to teach that the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה.

phrases.english: The sinner's meal offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: It has no oil or frankincense, yet it needs הגשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the oil-and-frankincense objection of Step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil and frankincense might be what causes the need for הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת חוטא has neither and still needs הגשה, so they are not the cause.

steps.title: Combining the two cases into a common element
steps.stepSummary: Since neither the מנחת העומר nor the מנחת חוטא can prove the point alone, the ברייתא combines them. Both need קמיצה and both need הגשה. The מנחת סוטה also needs קמיצה, so it should also need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the reasoning comes back around. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that both need קמיצה and both need הגשה. So I will bring the מנחת סוטה, which also needs קמיצה, and say it should also need הגשה!
steps.whatsHappening: Each earlier comparison was knocked down by itself. Now the ברייתא puts the מנחת העומר and the מנחת חוטא together to build a stronger proof for the מנחת סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone had a weakness: the מנחת חוטא is wheat, and the מנחת העומר has שמן and לבונה. Those weaknesses are different, and each one is cancelled by the other offering. So the only thing left in common is קמיצה, and the מנחת סוטה shares that.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning comes back around to the start
This case is not like that case; each has its own feature
The common element; a proof built from what two cases share
Taking a handful from the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צד השוה. When two weak sources cover each other's weak points, together they can prove something neither could prove alone.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around:
the aspect of this one is not like the aspect of that one,
and the aspect of that one is not like the aspect of this one.
The common element between them
is that they are equal in needing קמיצה and equal in needing הגשה.
So I too will bring the מנחת סוטה,
which is equal to them in needing קמיצה:
it should be equal to them in needing הגשה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two sources that each failed alone in steps 10 through 14
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared features of the מנחת העומר and the מנחת חוטא

steps.title: The common element has its own special feature
steps.stepSummary: The צד השוה is attacked. Both the מנחת העומר and the מנחת חוטא must be fine flour, but the מנחת סוטה may come as coarse flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the common element? Both of those offerings cannot come as coarse flour. Can you say the same about the מנחת סוטה, which may come as coarse flour?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds a feature that both source offerings share and the מנחת סוטה lacks. That breaks the צד השוה proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה only works if the shared feature is the only relevant one. Here there is a second shared feature: both must be fine flour. That could be the real reason they need הגשה, and the מנחת סוטה does not have it.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X, which has this special feature? Used to refute a proof
Were made fit or allowed
Coarse flour, not the fine סולת

phrases.english: What about the common element between them?
They are not fit to come as coarse flour.
phrases.notes: קמח here means rough, unsifted flour, as opposed to fine flour.

phrases.english: Will you say the same about the מנחת סוטה,
which is fit to come as coarse flour?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ לָבֹא קֶמַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the צד השוה built in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה proof for the מנחת סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both source offerings share a stricter feature, being fine flour, that the מנחת סוטה lacks.

steps.title: So a verse is needed for the מנחת סוטה
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot prove it, the פסוק ״וְהִקְרִיבָהּ״ teaches that the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says: ״וְהִקְרִיבָהּ״, "and he shall bring it near."
steps.whatsHappening: Every logical proof has failed, so the ברייתא concludes that we need a פסוק. The פסוק ״וְהִקְרִיבָהּ״ includes the מנחת סוטה in the rule of הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the payoff of the whole back-and-forth. The proofs were raised and rejected to show that the פסוק is not extra. It is truly needed to teach this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says; a verse brought to teach the rule
And he shall bring it near

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה only because of the פסוק ״וְהִקְרִיבָהּ״. Every logical proof failed. רבי יהודה learns it from ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״ instead (next step).

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "And he shall bring it near."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 16 broke the last logical proof, a verse is brought instead
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מנחת סוטה needs הגשה, learned from ״וְהִקְרִיבָהּ״

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source for the מנחת סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the מנחת סוטה from the word ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״, and backs this up with the פסוק in the סוטה section. He adds that the מנחת העומר needs no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״ comes to include the מנחת סוטה in the rule of הגשה. And so the פסוק says about סוטה: "and he shall bring her offering for her." But the מנחת העומר does not need a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion appears. רבי יהודה uses a different word in the פסוק, ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״, to teach that the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה points out that the סוטה section uses the same word, "bring." He then says the מנחת העומר needs no פסוק at all, which sets up the next question: why not?

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall bring
To include
And so the פסוק says; a supporting verse
A פסוק is not needed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "And you shall bring"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: comes to include the מנחת סוטה in the rule of bringing near.
And so it says:
"And he shall bring her offering for her."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:15. The same word, "bring," shows up in the סוטה section.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא,
phrases.english: But the מנחת העומר does not need a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״ – לְרַבּוֹת מִנְחַת סוֹטָה לְהַגָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק as the source for the מנחת סוטה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת סוטה needs הגשה, learned from ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״. The מנחת העומר needs no פסוק.

steps.title: Why does the מנחת העומר need no verse?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why רבי יהודה says the מנחת העומר needs no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. It asks how we know the מנחת העומר needs הגשה without a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A halacha usually needs a source. If there is no פסוק, there must be a logical proof, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's claim in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we know the מנחת העומר needs הגשה without a פסוק

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the מנחת חוטא teaches the מנחת העומר
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת חוטא has no תנופה and still needs הגשה. So the מנחת העומר, which does have תנופה, surely needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes from logic. The מנחת חוטא does not need תנופה, yet it needs הגשה. So the מנחת העומר, which does need תנופה, should surely need הגשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The מנחת העומר's need for הגשה comes from a קל וחומר, so no פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת חוטא is the "lighter" offering here, since it has no תנופה. Even so, it needs הגשה. The מנחת העומר is "heavier" because it has תנופה, so it should need הגשה all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned through logical reasoning
Is it not logical? Used to conclude a קל וחומר
Waving the offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of קל וחומר that was tried for the מנחת סוטה in step 10. It does not survive here either: step 21 knocks it down with the same wheat objection. The עומר is finally proven through the צד השוה in step 25.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the מנחת סוטה needs הגשה because of ״וְהֵבֵאתָ״. The מנחת העומר needs no פסוק because logic proves it. The proof opens with a קל וחומר from the מנחת חוטא, and the next steps turn it into a צד השוה.

phrases.english: It comes from logical reasoning:
Just as the meal offering of a sinner,
which does not need waving,
still needs bringing near,
then the מנחת העומר, which does need waving,
is it not logical that it needs bringing near!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדִּינָא קָא אָתְיָא: וּמָה מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה תְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עומר's הגשה is learned by logic, starting with a קל וחומר from the מנחת חוטא. That קל וחומר is challenged in step 21 and rebuilt as a הצד השוה in step 25.

steps.title: The sinner's offering is wheat, but the עומר is barley
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא attacks the proof from מנחת חוטא: it is made of wheat, while the מנחת העומר is barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the sinner's meal offering? It is special because it comes from wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pokes a hole in the proof from step 20. The מנחת חוטא is different from the מנחת העומר, so we cannot learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said that if the מנחת חוטא needs הגשה, the מנחת העומר surely does too. But the מנחת חוטא is made of wheat, and the עומר is made of barley. Maybe only wheat offerings, the more 'proper' kind of flour, need הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X? It is special because...' This is the standard way to show that a source is different from the case we want to learn.
The meal offering of a poor person who sinned
Wheat

phrases.english: What about the meal offering of a sinner?
It is special, because it comes from wheat.
phrases.notes: The hidden point is that the מנחת העומר is made of barley, so it is not the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁכֵּן בָּאָה חִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from מנחת חוטא to מנחת העומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is wheat and the target is barley. That difference may be the real reason the source needs הגשה.

steps.title: The סוטה offering shows that barley also needs הגשה
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת סוטה is barley and still needs הגשה, so being wheat is not the deciding factor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The meal offering of a סוטה proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the attack by pointing to a different offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת סוטה is made of barley, just like the עומר, and it still needs הגשה. So wheat is not the reason an offering needs הגשה, and the attack from step 21 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove.' Another case shows that the difference someone raised does not matter.
The barley meal offering brought by a woman suspected of adultery
Barley. Both the סוטה offering and the עומר are made of it.

phrases.english: The meal offering of a sota will prove it.
phrases.notes: The סוטה offering is barley and still needs הגשה, so barley is not a problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wheat-versus-barley attack.
steps.terutzMaskana: A barley offering (סוטה) also needs הגשה, so wheat is not the reason.

steps.title: The סוטה offering is special because it clarifies a sin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא attacks the new source: the מנחת סוטה is unique because it comes to clear up whether a sin happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the סוטה offering? It is special because it comes to clarify a sin, since it is called 'a reminder of sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא attacks the מנחת סוטה as a source, just as it attacked the מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה offering has a special job: it helps find out whether the woman sinned. The פסוק calls it 'a reminder of sin.' The עומר has no such job, so maybe that special job is why the סוטה offering needs הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: To clarify a sin, meaning to find out whether a sin happened
'A reminder of sin,' which is how the תורה describes the סוטה offering
Sin

phrases.english: What about the meal offering of a sota?
It is special, because it comes to clarify a sin,
since it is 'a reminder of sin'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:15

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִנְחַת סוֹטָה שֶׁכֵּן בָּאָה לְבָרֵר עָוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source brought in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the מנחת סוטה as a source for the עומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוטה offering has a unique purpose, clarifying a sin, which the עומר does not have.

steps.title: The sinner's offering shows that clarifying a sin is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: The מנחת חוטא does not clarify any sin and still needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sinner's meal offering proves otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to the first source to answer the attack on the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת חוטא is not brought to find out whether someone sinned, yet it needs הגשה. So clarifying a sin is not what makes an offering need הגשה. Each source now covers the weakness of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner
A meal offering made of flour
A 'sliding-scale' offering. The מנחת חוטא is its cheapest level, brought by a very poor person.

phrases.english: The meal offering of a sinner will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack of step 23 by using the source that was attacked in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an offering that clarifies sin needs הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחת חוטא clarifies no sin and still needs הגשה.

steps.title: The common feature of both offerings proves the עומר needs הגשה
steps.stepSummary: Each source has a weakness, but together they share קמיצה and הגשה. The עומר also has קמיצה, so it also needs הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The proof goes back to its starting point. One case is not like the other, and the other is not like the first. What they share is that both need קמיצה and both need הגשה. So I will bring the מנחת העומר, which is like them in needing קמיצה, and it will be like them in needing הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא combines the two sources into a צד השוה proof and concludes that the מנחת העומר needs הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone had a special feature that could explain its הגשה (wheat, clarifying a sin). Neither special feature is shared by both, so it cannot be the reason. What both do share is קמיצה, and the עומר has קמיצה too, so it should also have הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The proof goes back' to its start, now built from both sources together
'This one is not like that one.' Each source has its own special feature.
The shared feature of two sources, used as a proof
Taking a handful of the flour to burn on the altar
Bringing the meal offering near to the corner of the altar
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: A צד השוה works when every source has a weakness of its own, but the sources cover each other's weaknesses. What they all share then becomes the basis for the proof.

phrases.english: And the proof goes back to its start,
this case is not like that case,
and that case is not like this case,
what they have in common
is that they are alike in needing a handful removed,
and they are alike in needing bringing near.
So I will also bring the omer meal offering,
which is like them in needing a handful removed,
and it should be like them in needing bringing near.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two sources after each was attacked and defended.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By a צד השוה from מנחת חוטא and מנחת סוטה, the מנחת העומר needs הגשה.

steps.title: How could anyone knock down this proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what flaw anyone could find in the צד השוה, which explains why רבי שמעון needed a פסוק instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would you refute this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. If the logic works so well, why would anyone need a פסוק to teach that the עומר needs הגשה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned the עומר's הגשה from a פסוק, which suggests he thought the logic fails. The גמרא asks what weak spot he found in the צד השוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You refute,' meaning you find a flaw in a proof
A refutation, an attack that knocks down a proof
'And what' or 'and how'

phrases.english: And how would you refute it?
phrases.notes: The proof looks solid, so why did רבי שמעון need a פסוק for the עומר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the צד השוה of step 25 can be refuted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw in the צד השוה made רבי שמעון rely on a פסוק?

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the two sources are common offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון refutes the צד השוה: the סוטה and sinner's offerings are common, while the עומר comes only once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון refutes it like this: what about the shared feature of those two? They are common offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing the flaw רבי שמעון found in the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources share another feature: they can be brought many times a year. The עומר is brought only once a year. Maybe being common is the real reason they need הגשה, so the proof fails and a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Common, found often
Refutes
Like this

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon refutes it like this:
What about the common feature of those two?
They are special, because they are common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sources are common offerings and the עומר is not, so the צד השוה can be knocked down.
steps.whyThisMatters: A צד השוה fails whenever all its sources share a feature the new case lacks. That is why רבי שמעון needs a פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: actually the עומר is the more common one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the refutation: the עומר comes every year without fail, while the other offerings might never be brought at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? On the contrary, this one is more common. Those other offerings, sometimes you do not find them at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה does not accept רבי שמעון's attack, so for him the logic works and no פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה turns the argument around. The עומר is guaranteed every single year. A poor sinner or a סוטה might not show up at all, so the עומר is really the more 'common' offering, and the attack does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
More
Sometimes, at times
You find

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון says the עומר needs a פסוק because the two sources are 'common.' רבי יהודה says the עומר is even more common, so logic alone proves it needs הגשה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, how does he answer this?
On the contrary, this one is more common,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the מנחת העומר, which is brought every year without fail.

phrases.english: those others, there are times
when you do not find them at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַדְּרַבָּה, הָא מְצוּיָיה טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי שמעון's refutation from step 27, defending רבי יהודה's view that the עומר needs no פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי שמעון's refutation of the צד השוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Calling the sources 'common' is backwards. The עומר is guaranteed every year, while the others may never be brought.

steps.title: Maybe 'And you shall bring' teaches something else
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the word והבאת might not be about הגשה at all. Maybe it teaches that a private person can bring a different kind of מנחה beyond the five in the פרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'and you shall bring' is not about הגשה. Maybe it means a private person may donate a different kind of מנחה, beyond these five in the פרשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own use of והבאת for הגשה. It offers a different meaning the word could have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If והבאת were needed to allow an extra kind of private מנחה, it would no longer be free to teach הגשה. So the ברייתא must show this other reading is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps the verse is saying (a different meaning is being proposed)
'And you shall bring', the word used for הגשה
A private individual, as opposed to the community
Donates voluntarily

phrases.english: Or perhaps it does not say 'and you shall bring'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: except to teach that an individual may donate
and bring a different meal offering,
other than these that are in this section.
phrases.notes: 'These' are the five wheat מנחות listed in ויקרא פרק ב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא passage that tests how the פסוק of הגשה is read.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using והבאת as the source for הגשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could be needed for a different law: allowing a private person to bring an extra kind of מנחה.

steps.title: Logic that a private person could bring barley
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a reason to think a private person could donate a barley מנחה. The community brings both wheat and barley, so maybe a private person can too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes sense: the community brings a required wheat מנחה and a required barley מנחה. So a private person, who brings a donated wheat מנחה, could maybe bring a donated barley מנחה too?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up the suggestion in step 29 with a logical comparison. It compares the community to the individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community has a wheat offering and a barley offering. An individual has wheat offerings, so the logic says he should have barley as well. This makes the reading of step 29 seem reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical (a reasoned argument)
The community
A required offering
A voluntary offering
Barley

phrases.english: And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: צִיבּוּר מֵבִיא מִנְחָה מִן הַחִיטִּין חוֹבָה,
phrases.english: the community brings a required meal offering from wheat,
phrases.notes: This is the שתי הלחם of שבועות.

phrases.english: and brings a required meal offering from barley,
phrases.notes: This is the עומר.

phrases.english: so too an individual, who brings a meal offering
from wheat as a donation —
might he bring a meal offering
from barley as a donation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical basis for the alternative reading suggested in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That an individual might be allowed to donate a barley מנחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the community, which brings both wheat and barley מנחות

steps.title: The word 'these' limits private offerings to the five
steps.stepSummary: The word אלה teaches that a private person has only these five מנחות. That rules out a barley donation, so והבאת stays free to teach הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'these': I have only these.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 29 by pointing to the word אלה in the same פסוק. That word limits private מנחות to the five listed ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אלה already rules out a private barley מנחה, והבאת is not needed for that law. So והבאת can still teach הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (by saying)
I have only, a limiting phrase

phrases.english: The verse says 'these' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: I have only these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 29 and 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different word in the פסוק handles the proposed law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: והבאת might allow a private barley מנחה
steps.terutzMaskana: אלה limits private מנחות to the five, so והבאת teaches הגשה

steps.title: Maybe 'these' means bring all five
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests אלה might mean something else. Maybe someone who vows 'a מנחה' without saying which kind must bring all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'these' is about someone who says 'I take upon myself a מנחה', and it teaches that he must bring all five of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now challenges its reading of the word אלה. It offers a different law that word might teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלה means 'all of these', then a person who made a general vow would have to bring every kind. Then אלה would not be limiting the kinds of private מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I take upon myself a meal offering', a vow without saying which kind
All five of them

phrases.english: Or perhaps it does not say 'these'
except about one who says, 'I take upon myself a meal offering,'
that he brings all five of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of אלה used in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading אלה as a limit on private מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אלה could mean 'all of these', so a person with a general vow would owe all five.

steps.title: 'Of these' means he may choose
steps.stepSummary: The word מאלה, meaning 'of these', shows that he may bring one kind or all five, as he wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'of these': if he wants, he brings one; if he wants, he brings all five.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 32 from the exact wording מאלה. 'Of these' means some of them, not all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter מ in מאלה means 'from' or 'part of'. So the פסוק does not require all five. That leaves אלה free to limit private מנחות to these kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of these', meaning some of these
If he wants

phrases.english: The verse says 'of these' —
if he wants, he brings one;
if he wants, he brings all five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person who vowed 'a מנחה' must bring all five
steps.terutzMaskana: מאלה means he may bring just one, or all five if he wishes
steps.whatToRemember: והבאת teaches הגשה. אלה limits private מנחות to the five wheat kinds. מאלה means a general vow can be paid with just one kind.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: other מנחות also need הגשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from 'the מנחה' that other מנחות, such as those of non-Jews and of women, also need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'the meal offering' comes to include other meal offerings, like the מנחה of non-Jews and the מנחה of women, for הגשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives his own source from the פסוק. It extends הגשה to more types of מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words את המנחה are read as including more cases. Here רבי שמעון uses them for מנחות not listed in the פרשה, like those of non-Jews and women. The first part of the ברייתא used the same words for the מנחת חוטא, in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: To include more cases
A meal offering brought by a non-Jew
A meal offering brought by a woman
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
'the meal offering' — to include other meal offerings,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

phrases.english: such as the meal offering of non-Jews and the meal offering of women,
for bringing near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with רבי שמעון's reading of את המנחה, which extends הגשה to other מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Other מנחות, like those of non-Jews and women, need הגשה, learned from את המנחה.

steps.title: Should שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים be included too?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether this inclusion goes so far as to cover שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might I include even the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests how far רבי שמעון's inclusion reaches. It asks whether it covers two well-known bread offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If את המנחה includes 'other מנחות', it might seem to include every one. So the ברייתא asks whether שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים also need הגשה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think
The two loaves of שבועות
The showbread on the שולחן

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even the two loaves and the showbread?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the inclusion of step 34 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the inclusion from את המנחה reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Other מנחות' could cover every מנחה, even שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים.

steps.title: 'Of these' keeps them out
steps.stepSummary: The word מאלה limits the inclusion, so שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים do not need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'of these'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 35 with the limiting word מאלה. Not every מנחה is included in הגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: את המנחה includes more cases, and מאלה puts a limit on them. So the מנחות of non-Jews and women are included, but שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are not.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, את המנחה brings in the מנחות of non-Jews and women for הגשה, and מאלה keeps out שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים.
steps.confusionAlert: מאלה shows up twice in this passage with two different jobs. Before, it let someone pay a general vow with one kind. Here, רבי שמעון uses it to keep שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים out of הגשה.

phrases.english: The verse says 'of these'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים would also need הגשה
steps.terutzMaskana: מאלה excludes them, so they do not need הגשה

steps.title: Why include the other offerings but exclude the two loaves and the shewbread?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know which group the word מאלה excludes and which group it includes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to include the other מנחות and to exclude שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own last answer. Maybe we should do the opposite, and include שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים while excluding the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 36, מאלה limited the inclusion. A limiting word does not tell us by itself which offerings stay in and which go out. The ברייתא wants a reason for the split it made.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? This asks for the reason behind a choice.
To include
To exclude
The two loaves brought on שבועות
The shewbread placed on the שולחן each שבת

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the other meal offerings,
and to exclude the two loaves and the shewbread?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which way the limitation from Step 36 should go
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to exclude שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים rather than the other מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word includes and another limits, but nothing yet shows which group belongs on which side.

steps.title: Offerings with a part burned on the fire are included
steps.stepSummary: The other מנחות have a part burned on the מזבח, so they are included. שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים have no part burned, so they are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the other מנחות because part of them goes on the fire. I exclude שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים because none of them goes on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a logical reason for the split. Offerings with a part burned on the מזבח are more like the מנחות in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is whether part of the offering goes to the אישים, the fire on the מזבח. The other מנחות have a קמיצה that is burned, so they are similar to the listed מנחות. שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are eaten completely by the כהנים, so they do not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The fires of the מזבח
The other meal offerings
I include

phrases.english: I include the other meal offerings,
since some of them goes to the fires,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: and I exclude the two loaves and the shewbread,
since none of them goes to the fires.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי שְׁאָר מְנָחוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ מֵהֶן לָאִישִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 37
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical criterion: whether part of the offering is burned on the מזבח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have excluded the other מנחות and included שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Offerings with a part burned are included in הגשה. Offerings eaten completely are excluded.

steps.title: What about the libation offering, which is burned completely?
steps.stepSummary: By that reasoning, מנחת נסכים, which is burned entirely, should certainly need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But מנחת נסכים goes completely on the fire. Should it also need הגשה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses its own new rule to raise a problem. If going on the fire is the reason for הגשה, then מנחת נסכים should need it even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 made going to the fire the reason for including an offering. מנחת נסכים goes to the fire completely, more than the other מנחות do. So the rule seems to require הגשה for it as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering brought together with wine libations alongside a קרבן
Bringing the מנחה near to the corner of the מזבח
All of it
One might think

phrases.english: But isn't the libation meal offering entirely for the fires?
One might think it should require bringing near?
phrases.notes: Some versions have יהא (in round brackets). The corrected wording, in square brackets, is תהא, the feminine form that matches מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from Step 38 against itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that going to the fire is the reason for including an offering in הגשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחת נסכים goes to the fire completely, so by Step 38's rule it should certainly need הגשה.

steps.title: The word והקריבה excludes the libation offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says והקריבה, and this shows that מנחת נסכים does not need הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and it shall be brought near.' This teaches that מנחת נסכים is excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from a word in the פסוק. The word והקריבה limits הגשה so that מנחת נסכים is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would include מנחת נסכים, so the ברייתא needs a word in the פסוק to exclude it. The word והקריבה, with the ending 'it', points to a specific offering and leaves מנחת נסכים out.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
And he shall bring it near

phrases.english: The verse states: "And it shall be brought near."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 39
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק overrides the logical rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מנחת נסכים goes entirely to the fire, it should need הגשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: מנחת נסכים does not need הגשה, because of the word והקריבה.

steps.title: Wasn't that word already used for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא objects that the word והקריבה was already used for a different teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you already use this word for something else?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the answer in Step 40. One word should not be used for two different teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word והקריבה was used to include the מנחת סוטה in הגשה (steps 9 and 17). If it is already used up, it cannot also exclude מנחת נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: You already took it out, meaning you already used it for another teaching
But surely

phrases.english: But didn't you already use it?
phrases.notes: Literally, 'you already took it out': this word was already used earlier for another teaching about הגשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in Step 40
steps.kashyaTarget: Using והקריבה to exclude מנחת נסכים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word was already used for another teaching, so it is not free to teach this one too.

steps.title: The extra letter ה teaches the second lesson
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said והקריב but said והקריבה. The extra ה gives us one more teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could have said 'and he shall bring near,' but it said 'and he shall bring it near.' The extra letter teaches the exclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by finding extra wording in the פסוק. The basic word teaches one thing, and the extra ה teaches the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והקריב by itself is enough for the first teaching. The added ending ה, meaning 'it', is extra, so it can teach that מנחת נסכים is excluded. This way each teaching has its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bring near, without the ending 'it'

phrases.english: [It could have said] "and he shall bring near"; [it says] "and he shall bring it near."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets aren't in the גמרא but are assumed. The point is that the ה at the end is extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 41
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the word: the basic word teaches one thing, and the extra ending teaches another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word was already used, so it cannot exclude מנחת נסכים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra ה in והקריבה is a separate source that excludes מנחת נסכים.

steps.title: Why exclude the libation offering instead of the other offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא again asks how we know the exclusion applies to מנחת נסכים and not to the other מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to include the other מנחות and to exclude מנחת נסכים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks the same kind of question as in Step 37, now about מנחת נסכים. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ה excludes something, but it does not say what. Since מנחת נסכים seemed even more fitting for הגשה because it is burned completely, the ברייתא needs a reason to exclude it rather than the other מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations of wine poured on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 37. There the question was about שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים, which are not burned at all. Here it is about מנחת נסכים, which is burned completely.

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the other meal offerings
and to exclude the libation meal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת שְׁאָר מְנָחוֹת וּלְהוֹצִיא מִנְחַת נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which offering the extra ה from Step 42 should exclude
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to exclude מנחת נסכים with the extra ה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By Step 38's rule, מנחת נסכים goes to the fire the most, so why is it the one excluded?
